title: Triton fusion trades memory traffic for register and shared-memory pressure
summary: Fuse a bandwidth-bound reduction when its working set fits on chip; choose launch geometry using the compiled resource footprint.

hardware: The tutorial includes CUDA and HIP target-specific occupancy calculations; each device still needs qualification
software: triton-lang/triton at 4eda6cc91e86553a2517d1c764ea2967985553ad; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Rows fit the kernel resource envelope; the input stride and masked padded width are accounted for

claims.description: The fused softmax tutorial avoids intermediate global-memory passes and masks power-of-two padding.
Its launch calculation uses compiled register/shared-memory usage and distinguishes HIP occupancy. tl.exp is approximate.

downstream_impact: vLLM and vLLM-Omni: use profiler evidence to nominate elementwise/reduction chains for fusion; retain eager dtype/rounding contracts.
vllm-ascend: this CUDA/HIP tutorial is design input, not proof that its kernel runs on an NPU backend.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an OmniRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Test irregular widths, row strides and numerical extremes against the original operation sequence.
Sweep widths and measure traffic, occupancy/spills and latency before checking end-to-end effects.
limitations: Tutorial speedups are tied to its reference implementations and shapes; they are not predictions for current torch.compile or a service.
Fusion can regress when register pressure, padding or shared-memory demand reduces occupancy.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
